Open and close pores in leaves

questions.prompt: A cube-shaped cell has sides of 2 µm. What is its surface area ÷ volume ratio?
As a cube-shaped cell gets bigger, what happens to its surface-area-to-volume ratio?
questions.explain: Volume grows faster than surface area.

questions.prompt: Why is it a problem for a cell to be very large?
options: Its surface couldn't take in food and oxygen fast enough for its large volume
questions.explain: Materials enter and leave through the surface.
A single cell can carry out all life processes.

questions.prompt: Which is one of the largest single cells?
options: An ostrich egg (the yolk before it develops)
questions.explain: Unfertilised egg yolks of birds are single, very large cells.

questions.prompt: Scientists can now grow specialised cells, such as heart muscle or skin cells, in the lab. Suggest one benefit and one concern about using this technology in medicine.
questions.modelAnswer: Benefit: skin grown from a patient's own cells can treat severe burns without rejection, and lab-grown heart cells can be used to test new medicines safely, reducing animal testing. Concerns: the treatments are very expensive and may not be available to poor patients; long-term safety is not fully known; there are ethical questions about using some kinds of cells.
questions.explain: Criterion D: evaluate science and society.

questions.text: A cell that has a special shape and structure for a particular job is a ___ cell.
questions.explain: Specialisation lets multicellular organisms divide up the work.
